_doc: One entry per shipped model. Code finds models here (src/models.js), never by hard-coded tables. Convention: after 'rot' (Euler degrees, applied in 'order', default XYZ) the model faces +z (bow/head), up +y. 'fit' says where y = 0 goes: 'center' (animals: box centre at the origin, scaled so the length along z matches), 'bottom' (boats: lowest point at y = 0, then lowered by draft_m), 'base' (trees: base at y = 0, scaled by height). 'tint' is a per-species colour multiplier. A model with one file has 'file'; a model with detail tiers has 'files': { tier: { file, tris, bytes } } (tiers listed in 'tiers.order', best first; src/lod.js picks by distance and bakes the far impostor at run time). Files live in models/ as <file>.glb.txt (base64, what the published page fetches). 'bytes' is the size of that .glb.txt. Only slimmed files ship (textures <= 2k, webp). Tree tiers are made by tools/assets/node/treelod.mjs from the full model. Assets owns this file. Single-file models under ~1k triangles carry no tiers: LOD.tiersFor draws the mesh near and the baked impostor far. 'shadow': { tier, far_m } makes one tier (low) cast the shadow for every tier, in one draw, out to far_m from the camera (src/lod.js, LOD.shadowSource; trees, 31 Oct).

tiers._doc: Detail tiers a model may carry, best first. 'hd' ~25k tris (right by the boat), 'mid' ~6k, 'low' ~1.5k (card-culled foliage, grown to keep the crown's density). Past 'low' comes the impostor LOD.impostor bakes at run time, then nothing (the terrain's canopy texture). A model without a tier falls back to the next best it has.

textures._doc: Shared textures in textures/ (Assets). Layouts are in docs/facades.md. All of these are procedural stand-ins made by tools/assets/facades.py (CC0, this project) until photographs replace individual tiles; each tile is 2 m x 2 m of wall or roof and tiles seamlessly.

fill._doc: Mineral-fill swatch palette for the Critical Zone editor's fill brushes: textures/fill/palette.json (one entry per swatch: tiles, source, measured D50/sorting/roundedness/densities). Grouped by class. See textures/fill/README.md. Boulder/cobble classes also ship as individual de-lit clast stamps (textures/fill/clasts/) to be scattered, never tiled.

docks._doc: Docks are built by src/docks.js from a dock.json (docs/docks.md); styles in textures/dock/styles.json. Baked prefabs are listed as models with kind 'prefab'.

materials._doc: Terrain surface materials (Assets). One entry per material; textures/terrain/<id>/ holds colour.jpg (sRGB as photographed), normal.jpg (OpenGL tangent space), height.png (8-bit, stretched to the 0.5-99.5 % range of the source; height_range_src keeps that range in the source's 0..1 units) and rough.jpg, all 1024 px, seamless, made by tools/assets/terrainmats.py. tile_m = real-world width of one tile in metres (Poly Haven's measured dimensions). Packing for the terrain (no new samplers): array A (uRocks) layer = colour.rgb + height in alpha, array B (uRocksN) layer = normal.rgb + roughness in alpha, one layer per material, layers built from the ids a level uses. Masks and code name materials by id, never by layer index. formations = level geology class ids, habitats = habitat class ids this material suits. far_only materials are aerial tiles (30-90 m): sample them only in the far octave. Colour is as photographed elsewhere: the per-formation sets (terrain_sets) carry the Maine colour targets sampled from real material, which is how the colour rule is met. Legacy ids the editor already offers (rock, sand, cobble, forest, mud: the level's tex/*_diff.jpg) stay valid until World retires them.

terrain_sets._doc: Proposed material set per bedrock formation and per habitat for levels/downeast (Assets proposes, World adopts: the level manifest's geology classes get a "set" pointing here, see docs/terrain-materials.md). Roles: face = steep rock (slope >= ~35 deg, triplanar), ledge = bare rock below that slope, rubble = loose stone at the foot of faces and on boulder/cobble habitat, lichen = overlay above the spray zone (w = its maximum weight), far = replaces the far octave beyond ~250 m. Two materials in a role blend by low-frequency noise with weights w, which breaks the tiling. colour_target: the sampled Maine colour the set is graded toward (shader multiplies by target / material mean, luminance-preserving); null = not sampled yet, draw as photographed. Habitat "wet" = the material below mean high water (the shader still darkens and glosses wet ground; this only swaps the texture).

formations.name: Bar Harbor Formation
formations.note: Thin-bedded, jagged, layered. Both face materials carry straight beds along the texture u axis: project faces with rotation 0 so beds lie level (the formation dips gently; a per-class dip of ~10 deg would be the next refinement). marble_rock_03 on ledges breaks the bedding into the jagged blocks the Shore Path shows. gray_rocks (angular platy) is the talus. Ledge tops scale 1.0, faces 0.6 (thinner beds than the 2 m tiles).

formations.name: Cadillac Granite

colour_target.needs: Matt's photos of Otter Cliffs / Sand Beach headland / Thunder Hole ledge (dry, above the weed line, overcast); until then as photographed

formations.note: Coarse pink-grey, rounded, sheeted. tiger_rock (the coarse pink crystal grain) leads on the faces and dry_riverbed_rock (sub-horizontal sheet joints) is second: on tall cliff faces the jointed one repeated into a brick pattern, and the geometry now makes the sheets and joints itself (ledge brush, 18 Oct) (it is more saturated than Cadillac: the colour target will pull it down). Ledges: the coarse pink grain (tiger_rock) and the sheet joints (dry_riverbed_rock) both, so tops read as granite rather than marble; weathered grey comes from the lichen overlay (lichen_rock). marble_rock_01 was tried on the ledges and read as veined marble, so it is not in this set. Far octave: rocky_terrain (pink jointed slabs seen from 90 m) gives the ledge pattern from the water. Rubble: rounded granite cobbles.

_cutoff_doc: cutoff_m (every model, 18 Oct house rule): the distance in metres beyond which the model is not drawn at all (World and lod.js honour it; the terrain texture, canopy texture or nothing takes over). Default = 300 x the model's size (its length; for poles and gangways the square root of its silhouette area, so a 6 m piling 0.3 m thick counts as 1.3 m), where it shrinks to about 3 px on a 1080-line screen with the sim's 50 deg camera, clamped to 60..5000 m; trees 1200 m (where their impostors already stop today; the canopy texture beyond). lod.js LOD.tiersFor caps every tier's far at cutoff_m, so it only ever shortens what draws. Tune per model in docs/perf.md.
